mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 0.25% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4.0% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE < 4.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during two consecutive quarters of declining GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% from the previous month, sustained for two months, indicates supply chain stress, which raises costs and reduces margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when INDPRO falls by >0.5% for two months in a row.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.4% month-over-month, combined with a federal funds rate below 1%, signals inflationary pressure with accommodative policy, which initially boosts market sentiment and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: early inflationary regime with loose policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when CPIAUCSL > 0.4% and FEDFUNDS < 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 alongside an unemployment rate above 5% signals a recovery in labor market conditions, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when PAYEMS increases by >100,000 and UNRATE > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between the real savings rate (RSAFS) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days: higher household savings imply greater financial market participation and capital accumulation, supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: The correlation between RSAFS and S&P 500 60-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) over any 10-year rolling window.
